scenarios.claim: Callback identity changes whether a memoized child is invoked for an unrelated parent update.
scenarios.predicted: Inline callbacks invoke the memoized child again; stable callback variants do not.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React.memo compares function props by reference identity.
scenarios.nullCriterion: All four variants have the same child invocation count.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8, client render, memoized child, unrelated synchronous parent update.

scenarios.claim: The micro-timing ruler detects a deliberately larger synchronous render workload.
scenarios.predicted: Heavy work has a greater median micro total duration than light work.
scenarios.predictionBasis: The heavy variant executes more deterministic CPU work in render.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Heavy does not exceed light by the preregistered 0.25 ms threshold.
scenarios.applicability: Calibration only; not a React strategy claim.

scenarios.claim: The responsiveness ruler detects a deliberately planted main-thread block.
scenarios.predicted: The 80 ms block produces a larger maximum scheduling gap and at least one long task.
scenarios.predictionBasis: A synchronous busy loop prevents the 1 ms sampler from running.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The planted block produces no gap above 50 ms.
scenarios.applicability: Calibration only; timing depends on the recorded machine and Chrome build.

scenarios.claim: The frame sampler observes a deliberately presented intermediate state.
scenarios.predicted: The staged variant presents intermediate before final; direct presents only final.
scenarios.predictionBasis: The staged variant defers its second update until after an animation frame.
scenarios.nullCriterion: No intermediate frame is observed for staged.
scenarios.applicability: Chrome foreground page at the manifest viewport; frame counts use ranges.

scenarios.claim: The intra-variant gate rejects a tree whose two declared snapshots disagree.
scenarios.predicted: Consistent passes and planted-tear is rejected by the gate.
scenarios.predictionBasis: Cross-variant markup equality cannot prove agreement within one committed tree.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The planted inconsistent tree passes.
scenarios.applicability: Synthetic gate fixture; not evidence that React tears.

scenarios.claim: A zero-millisecond timer defines a stable browser task boundary.
scenarios.predicted: No claim: the row is retained to prove exclusion propagation.
scenarios.predictionBasis: Timer scheduling and rendering opportunities are race-sensitive.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Not applicable to an excluded row.
scenarios.applicability: Schema and publication control only.

exclusionReason.message: Retained as an excluded race row.

reasons.message: Retained as an excluded race row.

scenarios.claim: A React commit can occur without a DOM mutation, and component invocation, commit, and mutation counts are distinct signals.
scenarios.predicted: A constant-markup update invokes and commits once with no mutation; a forced round trip invokes and commits twice with two text mutations.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React may finish an update and commit a tree whose host output is unchanged; flushSync creates explicit commit boundaries.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The ruler cannot distinguish the planted no-mutation update from the planted mutation round trip.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 createRoot production build; synchronous updates in one host task.

scenarios.claim: State placement changes the scope of component invocation for the same leaf behavior.
scenarios.predicted: Local state invokes only the leaf; lifted state also invokes the parent and sibling.
scenarios.predictionBasis: A local state update begins at the owning leaf, while a parent-owned update re-invokes the parent subtree unless children bail out.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Local and lifted variants invoke the same component set.
scenarios.applicability: Unmemoized parent, leaf, and sibling in React 19.2.8 production.

scenarios.claim: React.memo only skips an unrelated parent update when the object prop retains reference identity.
scenarios.predicted: A stable object prop skips the memoized child; a recreated equal object invokes it.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React.memo performs shallow prop comparison using reference identity for objects.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Stable and recreated object props produce equal child invocation counts.
scenarios.applicability: React.memo with one object prop and an unrelated synchronous parent update.

scenarios.claim: Structural sharing lets a memoized unchanged branch skip work during an immutable update.
scenarios.predicted: Preserving the unchanged branch reference skips that branch; recreating it invokes both branches.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React.memo observes branch object identity at the prop boundary.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Preserved and recreated stable branches have equal invocation counts.
scenarios.applicability: Two memoized branch children receiving immutable object props.

intraVariant: changed branch is one and stable branch is zero

scenarios.claim: Updates within one callback batch together, while a real task boundary separates commits.
scenarios.predicted: Synchronous and same-microtask pairs commit once; updates split across timer tasks commit twice.
scenarios.predictionBasis: createRoot automatic batching groups updates in one callback, but does not merge separately completed task updates.
scenarios.nullCriterion: All execution contexts produce the same commit count.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 createRoot, functional updates, foreground Chrome task scheduling.

scenarios.claim: Repeated direct-value updates use one captured value, while functional updates compose through the queue.
scenarios.predicted: Three direct count+1 calls end at one; three functional increments end at three; each sequence commits once.
scenarios.predictionBasis: Direct updates enqueue replacement values computed from one render snapshot; updater functions receive queued intermediate state.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Direct and functional sequences end at the same count.
scenarios.applicability: Three synchronous updates issued from one render snapshot.

scenarios.claim: Same-value update behavior depends on whether real state work precedes it and whether a commit boundary intervenes.
scenarios.predicted: Fresh same-value updates do no render work; a post-commit same-value dispatch may add one invocation and one commit without a DOM mutation.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React can eagerly reject a same-value dispatch, while queued or recently committed work can still enter a render that later bails out.
scenarios.nullCriterion: All sequences have identical invocation and commit counts.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 useState in production; explicit animation-frame idle boundaries.

scenarios.claim: flushSync can create an extra commit without guaranteeing that the browser presents the intermediate DOM state.
scenarios.predicted: Automatic updates commit once; flushSync separation commits twice; intermediate presentation may range from zero to two sampled frames.
scenarios.predictionBasis: flushSync forces React DOM work before returning, while browser presentation still waits for a rendering opportunity.
scenarios.nullCriterion: flushSync does not change the commit count.
scenarios.applicability: Two synchronous state updates in one task; foreground Chrome frame sampling.

scenarios.claim: A Transition can time-slice expensive render work whose eventual host commit is small.
scenarios.predicted: The synchronous update creates a 100–300 ms scheduling gap; the Transition keeps maximum gaps below 50 ms while preserving final behavior.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React documents Transition rendering as non-blocking and interruptible; the workload performs CPU work in component bodies but changes one text node.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The Transition does not reduce the maximum scheduling gap below 50 ms in every rotation/process block.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production, 240 memoized null-returning items with 0.55 ms component-body work each.

scenarios.claim: Transition priority does not make synchronous commit-phase work interruptible.
scenarios.predicted: Both synchronous and Transition variants produce a 100–300 ms maximum gap and at least one Long Task from the 120 ms layout-effect block.
scenarios.predictionBasis: The component render is small, while the deliberately expensive public layout-effect boundary runs during commit before presentation.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Either variant avoids the planted commit-phase Long Task.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production with a deliberate 120 ms layout-effect block; calibration fixture, not normal application code.

scenarios.claim: An urgent state update can commit while a Transition render is incomplete, after which the Transition finishes.
scenarios.predicted: Transition-only commits once; urgent-interrupt commits urgent state before the final Transition commit and commits twice overall.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React documents that a Transition update may be interrupted by another state update and restarted afterward.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The urgent commit does not precede the Transition commit.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production; a flushSync urgent update is scheduled by a timer 12 ms into a 132 ms nominal Transition render workload.

intraVariant: displayed version and urgent state equal React state

scenarios.claim: Interrupted Transition component work can be executed and discarded before a later render commits.
scenarios.predicted: Uninterrupted has a zero discarded-work lower bound; interrupted has a positive lower bound while reaching its declared final state.
scenarios.predictionBasis: Repeated instrumented item invocations beyond one complete committed item set provide a conservative public lower bound on discarded work.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Interrupted work has a zero discarded-work lower bound.
scenarios.applicability: Instrumented lower bound only; it does not identify React work-loop units or internal discard locations.

intraVariant: displayed version and urgent state equal React state

scenarios.claim: Reading a mutable external store independently during a concurrent render can commit inconsistent values when the store changes between render chunks.
scenarios.predicted: The forced direct-read variant records the required external-mutation ordering and is rejected by the intra-tree tearing gate.
scenarios.predictionBasis: Independent reads are not tied to one React snapshot, so early and late items can observe different store versions.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The forced direct-read tree remains internally consistent or the mutation misses the render-chunk window.
scenarios.applicability: Forced host-timer mutation during a React 19.2.8 Transition; impurity negative control is not used.

intraVariant: final committed store values disagree as a planted tearing control

lifecycle.event: last render chunk of the first pass

scenarios.claim: useSyncExternalStore preserves intra-tree snapshot consistency when the store changes during a Transition render.
scenarios.predicted: The mutation lands between first-pass render chunks; React restarts before commit, and all committed values agree with a positive discarded-work lower bound.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React documents a pre-commit getSnapshot recheck and blocking restart when a store changes during a non-blocking Transition.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The committed tree tears, the mutation misses the window, or no restarted-work lower bound is observed.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production; stable subscribe/getSnapshot functions and a primitive immutable snapshot.

intraVariant: every observed commit and the final tree use one store version

scenarios.claim: useMemo skips stable-dependency recalculation, but timing benefit depends on the avoided calculation cost.
scenarios.predicted: Memoized variants perform zero update calculations; direct variants perform one. Expensive memoization wins every timing block, while the zero-work near-crossover pair may be inconclusive.
scenarios.predictionBasis: useMemo compares dependencies with Object.is and reuses the cached value; cache lookup overhead can be indistinguishable from trivial calculation cost.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Expensive memoization fails to beat direct calculation by 0.25 ms in every rotation/process block.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production; stable numeric dependency, zero-loop near workload, and 1,000,000-iteration expensive workload.

intraVariant: displayed tick and value equal state

reasons.message: Near-zero useMemo timing did not establish a stable direction above 0.05 ms.

scenarios.claim: Deriving display data during render avoids the extra commit caused by synchronizing redundant state in an Effect.
scenarios.predicted: Render-derived commits once; Effect-derived commits twice and runs one Effect setup; final behavior is equal.
scenarios.predictionBasis: An Effect runs after the source update commits and its state setter schedules another update.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Both variants have the same commit count.
scenarios.applicability: Client production render with a deterministic string derivation and a passive Effect synchronization variant.

scenarios.claim: A state update from a layout Effect adds a commit even when final behavior matches direct render derivation.
scenarios.predicted: Render-direct commits once; layout-effect commits twice with one setup.
scenarios.predictionBasis: useLayoutEffect runs during the commit boundary and a state update inside it is processed before paint.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The layout Effect does not add a commit.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production; one source update and one layout-Effect mirror update.

intraVariant: displayed source and mirror equal state

scenarios.claim: A state update from a passive Effect adds a commit even when final behavior matches direct render derivation.
scenarios.predicted: Render-direct commits once; passive-effect commits twice with one setup.
scenarios.predictionBasis: useEffect synchronizes the mirrored state after the source update, scheduling a second update.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The passive Effect does not add a commit.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production; one source update and one passive-Effect mirror update; no presentation claim.

intraVariant: displayed source and mirror equal state

scenarios.claim: When an Effect dependency changes, cleanup for the previous dependency precedes setup for the next dependency.
scenarios.predicted: The update logs exactly one cleanup followed by one setup and commits once.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React documents cleanup with old values before setup with new values after dependency changes.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Cleanup is missing or does not precede setup.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production passive Effect with one primitive dependency change.

scenarios.claim: A callback ref attaches during commit before the mounted child layout Effect runs.
scenarios.predicted: Mounting logs one ref attach before layout-effect setup and commits once.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React assigns DOM refs during the commit before layout Effects observe the mounted tree.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The ref does not attach before layout-effect setup.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production client mount with callback ref and child layout Effect.

intraVariant: child is mounted after the operation

scenarios.claim: Recreating an equal object dependency causes Effect cleanup/setup churn during an unrelated parent update.
scenarios.predicted: Stable dependency has no cleanup or setup; recreated dependency has one of each; final behavior is equal.
scenarios.predictionBasis: Effect dependencies are compared with Object.is, so an equal new object is different.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Stable and recreated dependencies have the same Effect lifecycle counts.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production passive Effect depending on one object prop.

scenarios.claim: Changing callback-ref identity detaches and reattaches the same DOM node during an unrelated parent update.
scenarios.predicted: Stable callback ref has no ref events; inline callback ref detaches once and attaches once; final behavior is equal.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React clears the previous callback ref and invokes the replacement callback when ref identity changes.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Stable and inline callback refs have the same attach/detach counts.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 production callback ref on one preserved DOM node.

scenarios.claim: Development Strict Mode replays render work, while root and subtree boundaries differ for the initial Effect replay.
scenarios.predicted: Production and plain development mount once; both Strict variants invoke render twice; only a Strict root replays the initial layout Effect.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React documents development-only Strict Mode render replay and the root-boundary exception for initial Effect replay.
scenarios.nullCriterion: Strict and non-Strict variants have identical mount invocation and Effect counts.
scenarios.applicability: React 19.2.8 client mount; separately bundled production/development realms; Strict Mode is development-only evidence.

scenarios.claim: The public Profiler callback is available in the profiling bundle but removed from the standard production bundle.
scenarios.predicted: Standard production records zero callback samples; the profiling build records one update callback.
scenarios.predictionBasis: React ships a dedicated profiling renderer build; standard production omits Profiler timing callbacks.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The profiling build records no callback or standard production records one.
scenarios.applicability: ReactDOM 19.2.8 standard production client entry versus react-dom/profiling, same subject workload.

scenarios.claim: Profiler instrumentation overhead must be quantified under the profiling build rather than assumed absent.
scenarios.predicted: Profiler-off records zero callbacks and Profiler-on records one; no preregistered timing winner is declared.
scenarios.predictionBasis: The profiling renderer gathers public timing data only when a Profiler boundary is present.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The instrument configurations cannot be distinguished by callback count.
scenarios.applicability: ReactDOM profiling build with a 500-component update; timing cells have explicitly different Profiler instruments.

scenarios.claim: Component-body work logging adds measurable apparatus work and must not contaminate normal timing passes.
scenarios.predicted: Work-log-on records the component-body instrument while work-log-off does not; final behavior remains equal and no timing winner is preregistered.
scenarios.predictionBasis: Recording 500 component invocations performs additional map and event-log work in the measured realm.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The instrument configurations are not isolated.
scenarios.applicability: Production build, 500 null-returning child components; timing cells intentionally differ by work-log instrumentation.

scenarios.claim: MutationObserver overhead must be measured with and without observation around the same React DOM update.
scenarios.predicted: Observer-on records the MutationObserver instrument while observer-off does not; final behavior remains equal and no timing winner is preregistered.
scenarios.predictionBasis: The observer-enabled cell asks the browser to create mutation records for 500 text updates.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The instrument configurations are not isolated.
scenarios.applicability: Production build, 500 text nodes; timing cells intentionally differ by MutationObserver instrumentation.

scenarios.claim: The responsiveness sampler and Long Task observer have their own overhead configuration and cannot be compared as micro timing.
scenarios.predicted: Instrument-off records two boundary ticks; instrument-on records at least 20 sampler ticks; final behavior remains equal.
scenarios.predictionBasis: The enabled cell runs a 1 ms interval and Long Task observer during the operation and 120 ms settling window.
scenarios.nullCriterion: The enabled sampler does not produce its required tick vector.
scenarios.applicability: Production build with 10 ms deterministic work; elapsed values are responsiveness-family measurements only.
